findings.F1: A sharp one-day fall is followed by a rebound. On the non-overlapping 3-day grid, the bars in the lowest decile of the past 1-day return (scaled by the 30-day volatility) are followed by a 3-day move of +2.04 % above the coin's drift. That is t 6.7 over 911 cases, positive in 18 of 19 coins, about 9 times the 0.22 % cost of a trade. The next decile shows only +0.25 % (t 0.97), and the middle deciles are negative (-0.13 to -0.92 %).
findings.F2: The rebound after a sharp one-day fall is much larger when recent volatility has expanded. In the lowest 1-day quintile, the bars with the top quintile of 5-day over 30-day volatility are followed by +3.17 % above drift (t 7.0, 460 cases, 18 of 19 coins). The other bars in that quintile show +0.46 % (t 1.9, 1362 cases). Across all bars, the top volatility-ratio quintile alone gives +1.09 % (t 4.5, 17 of 19 coins).
findings.F3: The rebound after a sharp one-day fall holds in every era and in both trends. By era it is +0.94 % (t 2.0) up to 2020, +1.80 % (t 3.7) over <date> and +0.90 % (t 3.3) from 2023, all above drift. It is larger when the coin's 30-day return is positive: +2.10 % (t 6.1, 811 cases) against +0.38 % (t 1.5, 1011 cases).
findings.F4: A downward break after a narrow 2-day stretch is followed by a fall, and the effect is strongest in a falling month, not the rising month the tested idea used. With the 30-day return negative, breaks in the narrowest quartile are followed by -1.61 % against drift (t -5.3, 795 cases, only 1 of 19 coins up). The rising-month version gives -0.50 % (t -1.4, 431 cases), which matches the inconclusive verdict.
findings.F5: In falling months, the move after a downward break is graded by how narrow the preceding stretch was. Over 3 days against drift it is -1.61 % (t -5.3) for the narrowest quartile, -0.64 % (t -1.9) for the second, +0.24 % (t 0.6) for the third and +0.78 % (t 2.3) for the widest. For the narrowest quartile, the effect appears in every era: -1.01 % (t -2.1), -1.56 % (t -3.3) and -1.10 % (t -3.1).
findings.F6: A downward break after a wide 2-day stretch is followed by a rebound. The widest decile of such breaks shows +2.51 % against drift (t 5.1, 491 cases, 17 of 19 coins). Within the widest quartile, the rebound is largest after the deepest 2-day falls: +1.34 % (t 3.6, 781 cases). This is largely the same situation as F1.
findings.F7: Narrow stretches are not followed by larger moves, against the brief's premise. The mean absolute 3-day move is 5.85 % after the narrowest fifth of 2-day stretches, against 6.75 % after the widest fifth. Upward breaks show no grading by narrowness: every quartile lies between -0.01 % and +0.20 %, with |t| < 1.

ideas.idea: After a coin's 1-day return is a large fall compared with its 30-day volatility, the coin rises more than usual over the next 3 days. The rise is larger the larger that fall, and larger still the more its 5-day volatility exceeds its 30-day volatility.
ideas.consequence: A trader should buy, or at least refuse to short, a coin right after a sharp one-day drop in a volatility spike, where the 3-day rebound is several times the cost of a trade.
ideas.name: rebound after sharp daily fall

ideas.idea: While a coin's 30-day return is negative, a 4-hour close below the lowest low of the preceding 2 days is followed by a fall over the next 3 days. The narrower those 2 days' range was compared with the coin's 30-day average 4-hour range, the larger the fall.
ideas.consequence: A trader should short quiet-range breakdowns in coins that fell over the past month, and refuse the same short when the preceding range was wide.
ideas.name: quiet breakdown in falling month
